description: Installed execution and durability policy. Optional computational recovery is separate from authoritative evidence, owner continuity and external-effect safety. This is not a caller-selectable authority object.

RecoveryPolicy.description: Owner-local closed configuration, selected independently of requests. The replay target is soft; fraction limits admission against estimates, not arbitrary-stall wall time. The attempt cap counts reserved/started attempts including failures. Retention applies only to unpinned optional derived generations. All numbers must also satisfy the installed finite interoperable JSON profile.

Rules.description: Normative repo-wide durability semantics carried in installed schema identities, not submitted or authenticated by a client object. Owners implement these rules at their existing boundaries.

const.scope: This is the common execution/durability contract for all owners, clients, reusable packages, supplied adapters and optional applications. Optimize successful-run elapsed time while preserving complete accepted evidence, current authority and safe effects. A semantic step, bounded execution yield, database transaction, authoritative commitment and optional recovery checkpoint are distinct boundaries. No implementation may infer one durable event per item, page, phase, poll, helper return or yield merely from boundedness or resumability. The policy neither enables an unimplemented capability nor qualifies a native storage, authority, supervisor or recovery profile.
const.state_classes: Classify state by its obligation rather than its name or storage engine. Semantic evidence includes exact accepted bytes, identities, observations, requests, preimages, results and custody facts at their promised retention boundary. Correctness-critical durable state is the minimum state necessary to preserve those obligations and safely explain, reconcile and control effects through declared failures. Optional recovery state is independently reconstructible derived state retained solely to save safe recomputation. Volatile state is bounded working memory, owner-private scratch/spill, scheduling and advisory progress without a durability promise. Sole custody, an acknowledged obligation, original randomness or an uncertain effect cannot be relabeled optional because its containing table appears rebuildable. The same physical transaction may protect several obligations; these categories do not mandate separate stores or separate writes.
const.checkpoint_meanings: An independent owner continuity checkpoint, signed workflow event/round/certificate, capture, backup/recovery point, protected restoration commit, accepted transfer offset or other user-visible durable result is not an optional computational checkpoint. Its owning safety contract continues to apply even for subsecond work and in restart mode. Optional generation count/retention limits never prune accepted journal events, recovery readers, backup retention, immutable evidence, held resources or protected state fixtures. A method named snapshot or checkpoint does not by itself decide the classification. An explicit requested backup or complete audit remains useful product work, not optional checkpoint overhead; repeatedly producing it merely for internal progress is not justified by that name.
const.necessary_barriers: Each durable boundary must identify its owner, protected obligation, declared failure model, retained replay inputs, earliest necessary persistence point and a concrete failure counterexample if removed or coalesced. Preserve acceptance before acknowledgement and effects; stable request/attempt identity and exact parameters before ambiguous native dispatch; appropriate preimage, first-write and source custody; positive one-writer exclusion, independently current permission, capacity debit and one-use launch; verified outcomes before dependent effects, success or custody/resource release. Unknown effects and cumulative confirmed facts survive retries, cancellation and restoration. Timeout, process-return, expired leases, DNS withdrawal and a cancelled future are not positive cessation. Classifying a barrier as mandatory does not justify per-item granularity: review safe grouping and reuse of existing exact durable anchors as well as its removal.
const.batching_and_visibility: Internal phase fusion, bounded batching, group commit and coarser replay frontiers are permitted without a new policy exemption when all actual semantic, authority, evidence and visibility obligations remain satisfied. Within one owner, one durable commit can cover an exact bounded ordered prefix of independently identifiable events; acknowledge each only after its bytes, results and required independent continuity commitment are durable. Grouping cannot cross a causal boundary whose dependent effect, peer vote or acknowledgement already requires the prior commitment. Do not start effects speculatively, invent cross-owner atomicity, merge independently current owners, or return from a commit-before-return interface before commitment. Keep original event identity, replay, conflict detection and discovery. The current append API is synchronous; its particular syscall count and internal flush layout are not the minimum native protocol. Do not deliberately hold a cheap operation waiting to fill a batch or earn credits. Changes to public signed evidence or causal decisions still require an explicit contract review; private computation traces and exact old interruption positions are not public invariants.
const.replay_domains: A replay domain is a dependency-consistent unit of unaccepted derived work recoverable from retained authoritative inputs and outcomes. It may span internal phases. Safe replay retains or faithfully reproduces the exact source/configuration/algorithm selection, original random identities, timestamps and nondeterministic observations required by the accepted semantics. It preserves stable idempotency identity and exact native parameters; unknown effects are reconciled, never blindly repeated under a new request identity. No checkpoint may become sole custody of an authoritative fact or authorize source release. Cached immutable validation may be reused within a proved identity/invalidation lifetime, but old positive authorization, native observations and restored snapshots confer no present permission. Resume requires current owner authority, fencing and input binding. Changed inputs or algorithms require a proved compatible reader or safe recomputation, never silent adoption. A cheap computation is not necessarily a safe restart of its surrounding effectful operation.
const.configuration: RecoveryPolicy is independently selected installed-owner configuration, not a caller-provided permission or application-source override. The closed default is adaptive, a 120-second soft replay target, a 0.125 optional-overhead fraction, no lifetime attempt cap and two usable generations. restart, zero fraction or zero attempt limit disables optional saves only. Bind effective policy and its installed revision to the logical execution through existing owner admission/anchor custody, outside accepted request/payload identity. Apply operator changes to new executions; an existing execution changes only through an explicitly reviewed safe update contract. No new RPC, source field, per-turn policy write or central configuration authority is implied. Invalid configuration rejects selection, not previously accepted custody. A retained policy never supplies current authority. Native implementations use the common decision semantics rather than independent slightly different thresholds; equivalent implementations must pass the same boundary cases.
const.quantities: All decision times are finite, nonnegative seconds with declared measurement/estimation provenance. S is conservative net recomputation time saved by the candidate relative to the existing valid frontier, after candidate load/revalidation cost; only completed covered useful work counts. U is cumulative useful non-optional elapsed work credited once to the logical execution, not parallel worker sums, CPU totals, queue wait, artificial sleep, idle polls, repeated replay or optional-overhead time. S cannot exceed credited U. C is a conservative admitted estimate of incremental checkpoint preparation, capture, representation, consistency, persistence, coordination and attributable reclamation. O is already charged optional cost plus outstanding disjoint reservations, including failed saves and unfinished lifecycle costs. Restore cost is subtracted in S, not charged twice. R is remaining useful time to completion or the next usable mandatory anchor, when known. Missing cost/remaining estimates are unknown, never zero. Native budget reservations may conservatively sum blocking costs but are not reported as measured critical-path time. Counters and calibrated cost profiles must be bounded; no per-record durable metering or repeated full-state measurement is required. Cost estimates include the cost of maintaining the optional recovery machinery itself.
const.admission: At an existing bounded safe boundary, perform ready completion or required durable work first; never insert a redundant final optional save. Otherwise require safely replayable inputs, a dependency-consistent candidate, admitted snapshot storage/resources, known bounded cost, complete conservative accounting, no conflicting save in that domain, and available policy/count allowance. Prefer finishing when known R <= C. Let beta be max_optional_overhead_fraction and b=beta/(1-beta). Simultaneously require S >= replay_target_seconds, C <= b*S, and O+C <= b*U. At the default this is S >= 120, 7*C <= S and 7*(O+C) <= U. If any test fails, continue useful work and reassess at a later safe boundary; do not wait to accumulate credit, abort correct work, drop extent or skip a mandatory barrier. A newly long execution can become eligible without its original duration prediction. The target is not a hard maximum-loss bound: cost, capacity, sparse safe boundaries, unknown estimates or configured caps may increase replay exposure. Report that tradeoff. No assumed failure rate, fixed checkpoint count per workflow type or target spending percentage is required.
const.reservations_and_failures: A positive pure decision is not a reservation. Under the existing current owner exclusion, recheck the same logical budget, policy, candidate generation and domain, then reserve its complete admitted cost before starting. Deduct any existing child grant once, never charge a parent reservation again when converting it to child actual cost. max_optional_checkpoints caps admitted attempts, including in-flight and failed attempts, not just successful publications; a failure cannot buy an unlimited retry loop. Charge actual attempt cost and retain reserves for unfinished associated cleanup. Only success advances the covered recovery frontier; failure preserves the previous usable frontier and charges its cost. An actual overrun creates debt and revises later estimates; underfunded optional work waits for real new useful credit. Never cancel a safety commit to enforce a timing ratio. If optional work causes capacity failure or damages authoritative custody, ordinary safety failure rules apply; it is not excused as a performance observation.
const.composition_and_restart: One logical operation or cross-owner workflow has one composable optional budget, not a new beta allowance for each phase, adapter, retry, process, child or participant. Independent user operations have independent budgets. Existing owners use disjoint allocations and conservative once-only elapsed credit; overlapping work cannot be counted twice. An existing workflow gate may allocate optional budgets but is not authority over another owner, and optional accounting adds no mandatory off-host service or synchronous participant round. Without a valid disjoint allocation or trustworthy composed accounting, suppress optional saves and continue mandatory/local work. Unused credit can be conservatively forgone; it cannot be manufactured by component splitting. Persist only the needed summary with existing anchors. Following interruption, restore/reconcile credits, charges, outstanding reservations and attempt counts conservatively; missing accounting disables optional saves until reconciled. Replayed work earns no fresh useful credit. An advisory counter does not require a new synchronous journal; fail closed for optional spending, not for safe execution or independent recovery.
const.execution_and_growth: Keep execution, memory, bytes, pages, cancellation responsiveness and scratch admission bounded independently of checkpoint cadence. Use owner-private spill for large working sets; a yield need not serialize state. Do not replace many small commits with an unbounded shared writer transaction held during validation, native calls, network waits or long CPU work. Required renewal, fences and cancellation remain responsive. Avoid setting up an optional resume store for cheap work merely to preserve a private API. Native state changes stay short, fenced and causally correct. All optional capture, hashing, copying, reservation, publication, restoration and cleanup work counts toward existing complete-extent and aggregate growth proofs. Repeated full-history snapshots are not justified by calling the output new input. Required historical restoration work is charged under the actual fixed failure schedule, not an impossible arbitrary-restart constant. The same semantic executor and validation obligations apply in restart and adaptive modes.
const.generation_integrity: An optional generation binds exact input/configuration/algorithm identity, owner/domain and covered dependency frontier to matching derived state and durable effect outcomes. A cursor ahead of its state is unusable. Build privately, durably establish complete required dependencies and atomically publish selection using qualified backend primitives. Preserve the prior usable generation through failure and later scratch writes; a flush of the only database after using unsafe synchronization is not that guarantee. Missing, torn, corrupt or incompatible optional state falls back to another valid anchor or safe recomputation; it never repairs or demotes corrupt authoritative history. Loading an optional generation cannot replay a native effect or restore authority. Success of a local save does not promise survival of destruction of its only device; software exception injection does not qualify power-loss behavior. Keep backend, failure domain and restore guarantees explicit.
const.retention_and_lifecycle: Keep the latest usable optional generation and its predecessor by default, plus dependencies and generations pinned by live readers within explicit resource admission. The retention target is not permission to delete a pinned generation, sole custody or accepted evidence. Retire only after actual reader/worker receipt and dependency release; cancellation requests are not quiescence. Admit the temporary space for old and new generations together. When space is unavailable, prefer replay rather than evicting required custody. Creation count, generation count and storage bytes are separate controls. Lifetime count/retention limits reduce resumability only, never the accepted collection, history, number of participants or complete-result extent.
const.workflow_application: Source intake, planning, validation, inspection, index rebuild and pure artifact preparation normally start without optional saves; retain any irreplaceable observations before accepting them. Installation and content delivery preserve sealed input, executable custody and acknowledged bytes while temporary recomputation follows this policy. Owner admission, adapter approval/dispatch, resource queues, grants and launches preserve authoritative decisions before acknowledgement/effects; progress and repeated polls are not automatically durable decisions. Scheduled work retains exact due-occurrence/child identity and avoids duplicate dispatch; backlog traversal can use optional recovery. Capture, backup, restore, relocation, credential rotation and DNS/ingress/network changes retain native preimages, first-write awareness, cutover evidence, current fences and positive release. Verification/recovery readers and optional directory/reporting/receipts services may recompute derived indexes but preserve their own acknowledged records. Absence of optional services cannot become an execution, authorization or recovery prerequisite. This common policy changes no independent owner boundary and introduces no generic distributed transaction or workflow engine.
const.measurement_and_qualification: Correctness of policy admission and accounting is a deterministic contract; actual machine-dependent latency is a measured observation, not a new numerical validation gate or a guaranteed beta ceiling under arbitrary storage stalls. Preserve existing correctness, growth, state, extent and evidence gates. Measure matched restart-mode and adaptive-mode executions with identical inputs, semantic validation and required safety barriers, plus any preserved baseline under equivalent conditions. Separate useful work, mandatory barrier cost, optional cost, provider waiting and interruption/recovery. Report accepted-result latency and complete lifecycle cleanup, including descendants and deferred work with explicit measurement scope; overlapping durations cannot be summed as wall time. Use existing profiling/evidence channels. Test boundary arithmetic, stale/duplicate reservations, restart accounting, domain coverage, failed saves, capacity, generation integrity and every mandatory effect/acknowledgement boundary with independent witnesses. Simulation proves only its scope; no native qualification follows from a policy helper. Unavailable cost profiles and systematic overruns remain visible improvement/implementation obligations, not blanket permission to disable adaptive recovery for all large supported work. Such findings do not create a new whole-repository approval-to-proceed or timing gate.
const.contract_change_and_custody: Review actual safety promises rather than preserving private phase counts, per-step progress or existing test traces as invariants. A coarser execution design must preserve complete semantic validation, public rejection behavior and meaningful causal ordering, not necessarily the private point of interruption. Update affected source-owned tests and interface/engineering projections together. This policy does not authorize deleting accepted data, changing protected commitments, rewriting introduced migration revisions or fixtures, discarding retained readers, disabling qualified synchronization on authoritative stores, or weakening branch/release gates. Keep state ownership, explicit initialization, forward-only upgrades, current authorization and protected failure handling. Review any genuinely incompatible public decision explicitly; no compatibility shim is required for an abandoned unprotected pre-v1 computation mechanism. No new product authority, native mutation or production release is enabled by this contract.
